extracted.intended_audience: periodical essayists and general authors (writers of short moral/observational papers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing brief, self-contained periodical essays (Spectator-style) that instruct and amuse; emphasizes concision, unity of thought, moral purpose, and avoidance of partisan or scurrilous attacks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheet as a self-contained treatise
rubrics_metrics.description: Every Sheet should be a kind of Treatise, and make out in Thought what it wants in Bulk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each short paper ought to present a complete, self-sufficient argument or meditation despite its small physical size — the piece should stand alone as a coherent unit of thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work up a point in all its parts
rubrics_metrics.description: That a Point of Humour should be worked up in all its Parts; and a Subject touched upon in its most essential Articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop the central idea thoroughly within the short form: pursue the humorous or thematic point through its aspects so readers feel the piece has covered the subject's essentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concision — the chymical method / quintessence
rubrics_metrics.description: An Essay-Writer must practise in the Chymical Method, and give the Virtue of a full Draught in a few Drops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to distill a larger thought into a small, potent piece. Prefer concentrated expression — provide the power or effect of a longer work in far fewer words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid repetitions, tautologies, and enlargements
rubrics_metrics.description: Without the Repetitions, Tautologies and Enlargements, that are indulged to longer Labours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not pad short pieces with needless reiteration or verbose expansion; eliminate redundancy so the essay remains sharp and compact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on essential aspects of the subject
rubrics_metrics.description: A Subject touched upon in its most essential Articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select and present only the most important facets of a topic appropriate to the brief form; omit peripheral digressions that do not serve the central point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim to instruct in wisdom and virtue rather than mere politics
rubrics_metrics.description: It were more advantageous to Mankind, to be instructed in Wisdom and Virtue, than in Politicks; and to be made good Fathers, Husbands and Sons, than Counsellors and Statesmen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize moral instruction, practical virtue, and the improvement of private life and manners over partisan political advocacy when choosing subjects and tones for periodical essays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diffuse knowledge so it is accessible and useful to the public
rubrics_metrics.description: Our common Prints would be of great Use were they thus calculated to diffuse good Sense through the Bulk of a People, to clear up their Understandings, animate their Minds with Virtue, dissipate the Sorrows of a heavy Heart, or unbend the Mind from its more severe Employments with innocent Amusements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write in a way that brings useful ideas into public conversation and everyday assemblies; aim to enlighten, console, entertain innocently, and make wisdom widely available rather than confined to learned libraries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not tailor writing to ignorant or malicious readers ('moles')
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not therefore for the Benefit of Moles that I publish these my daily Essays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that some readers lack taste or are motivated by envy; do not let the existence of ignorant or hostile audiences dictate the quality or purpose of your writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid partisan rancour and party spirit in tone and judgement
rubrics_metrics.description: I have endeavoured as much as I am able to extinguish that pernicious Spirit of Passion and Prejudice, which rages with the same Violence in all Parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eschew hot partisan temper, rancour, and factional bias in essays; strive for impartiality, reasoned judgment, and moderation rather than contributing to civil division.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use scurrility or abusive partisan style as substitute for satire
rubrics_metrics.description: An Abusive Scurrilous Style passes for Satyr, and a dull Scheme of Party Notions is called fine Writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resist the temptation to cloak partisan abuse in the name of satire. True wit and satirical value are not achieved through scurrility or partisan sloganeering; value writing by merit, not factional alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid building arguments on calumnies and unproven rumours
rubrics_metrics.description: Calumnies that have been never proved, or have been often refuted, are the ordinary Postulatums of these infamous Scriblers... When they have laid these Foundations of Scurrility, it is no wonder that their Superstructure is every way answerable to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not accept or propagate scandalous stories as established truth; avoid grounding pieces on doubtful or refuted assertions — this is an anti-pattern that corrupts judgment and discourse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge works by merit, not by party affiliation
rubrics_metrics.description: There is scarce a Person of any Figure in England, who does not go by two contrary Characters... Books are valued upon the like Considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate writing and authors on intrinsic quality rather than partisan identity; resist assigning praise or blame chiefly because of political sympathies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uphold plain truth and common-sense propositions
rubrics_metrics.description: This neutral Body should act with a Regard to nothing but Truth and Equity... That we do in our Consciences believe two and two make four; ... That it is our Resolution as long as we live to call Black black, and White white.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commit publicly to basic truths and equity; cultivate a plain-speaking, common-sense standard in essays so they serve as a corrective against confusion, sophistry, and deliberate falsehood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use satire and humorous social observation to correct folly
rubrics_metrics.description: I believe you will not think it below you, on so extraordinary an Occasion, to Unhoop the Fair Sex, and cure this fashionable Tympany that is got among them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ light satire and amusing social sketches (e.g., on fashion or manners) to expose and correct absurdities; temper correction with humor and avoid mean-spiritedness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ classical, historical, and natural-history allusions as illustrative devices
rubrics_metrics.description: When Knowledge... I cannot forbear reflecting upon that Passage in the Proverbs: Wisdom crieth... I remember to have read in Diodorus Siculus an Account... Natural Historians observe...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use brief classical, biblical, historical, or natural analogies and fables to reinforce moral points and lend authority or wit to short essays; draw examples from antiquity and nature to illuminate contemporary subjects.
